chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: Rex Stewart at LeCoco's in Redondo Beach and the unpaid salary
summary: Rex Stewart, without an embouchure, fronted a combo and pocketed Simmons's pay until the owner found out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Uh-huh. So I got so that I just stopped looking for jobs, you know. And finally, Rex Stewart -- boy, you're talking about off the wall. He had a job out at LeCoco's Supper Club.
In Redondo Beach. Right on the -- what was the main street? Sepulveda?

Pacific Coast Highway. And Rex had a combo down there, him playing trumpet, piano player and drums. And at this time, Rex didn't have any embouchure. He couldn't play a one chorus melody without muffing a note, you know, splitting a note or something. And then he'd let the piano player finish it out. And he was just there fronting and jiving. And Christmas week comes up and he tells me, he says, 'Bring your bass out and sit in with us and maybe make yourself a job and we'll give you what the kitty makes, and if that isn't enough we'll -- I'll take a couple of dollars out of my pocket.' You know. See, and let him hear how it sounds with the bass player.

So for the first week, Christmas week up to New Years, I'm getting kitty money. So New Years night, I told Mr. LeCoco, I said, "Well, I won't be seeing you any more." I said, "I've been here a week, and I think that's time enough for you to decide whether you're going to hire me or not." He said, "What do you mean?" He said, "I hired you the first night." And he had been giving Rex my salary all this time. He said, "Wait a minute." He called Rex. He says, "Rex," he said, "I've been giving you this man's money and you haven't been paying him?" Rex got real busy and he said, "Wait just a minute. I'll be right back." He went borrowing money all over the place, from his admirers and the band and everyone else, to get out of that hole. So he paid me in front of Mr. LeCoco. And we worked another week, and I went over to Rex's apartment. He was the caretaker of these units. I forget the girl's name that owned them. She was a dear friend of his.
